text: The Bhagavad Gita is meant for applying the principles in daily life. If you cannot, there is no point in reading the Gita. It is not just theory, it is a practical text on how to move forward.
author: Sri M

text: The great Kabir Das said many hundred years ago, 'kal karey so aaj kar, aaj karey so ab' meaning, 'What you are to do tomorrow, do it today, and what you should do today, do it right now!!' Postponement always ends in failure.
author: Sri M

text: When it comes to how to make the mind one pointed and free it from agitations that constantly assail it, the Yoga Sutras of Patanjali say there is only one way : 'Nairantarya Deergha Kale Abhyaasa,' which means 'Practice, practice, practice for a long, long time.
author: Sri M

text: The mind is fickle and difficult to control; it is always moving and turbulent, but we can bring it under control through effort, dispassion, and spiritual practice. Through constant practice of meditation, one can make the mind tranquil.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not just physical exercise, but according to the Bhagavad Gita every approach to life is Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: Thoughts can condition you and make you think that 'you cannot do something,' and thoughts can also be conditioned to say, 'Yes, I can do it!
author: Sri M

text: If Truth is infinite, if those who have touched it have said it is infinite, there must be infinite ways of finding it. Therefore, in all the 18 chapters of the Gita, different ways have been prescribed on how to arrive at the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishad declares that one who is most intelligent, very soon discovers the limitations of his intellect. Because, what the Upanishad is talking about, is something which is beyond even the understanding of our ordinary mind.
author: Sri M

text: For understanding of the Supreme Brahman, you are required to change your mind, and make it ready for it. The ordinary mind cannot understand this concept, because it is beyond the understanding of the senses.
author: Sri M

text: The philosophy of yoga says that the ordinary mind, which is always caught up in tensions, ups and downs, success and failure, cannot find the Truth. The mind has to settle down, and yoga is the tool for that.
author: Sri M

text: It’s only when the inner being becomes full of joy that the world becomes full of joy.
author: Sri M

text: When you begin to help others wholeheartedly, without looking for profit or loss, then you are no longer thinking only of yourself, you are moving out of your selfishness and your mind is expanding. Through service, through helping those who are unfortunate, we can expand our minds and reach the Supreme Truth.
author: Sri M

text: The Upanishads say that purna - fulfilment, fullness, and completeness - is the essential characteristic of one’s true being, which is one’s own consciousness, free of all distractions, and is called the Atman . When this Atman , or real Self - the core of the consciousness of every human being - is discovered, one reaches a state of perfect happiness and realises that it exists in every living being, though it often remains untapped.
author: Sri M

text: A sadhak who turns within to find the truth, which is his own Self, need not neglect the world or run away from it. This search for happiness, or for one’s identity or consciousness, is not reserved for renunciants, monks, or sannyāsins. It is for every human being who lives in this world, works for a living, has a family, and cares for other human beings.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana means spiritual practice. To become a Yogi, you don't have to change your clothes or your hairstyle. You don't have to wear Rudrakshas. None of these things are required for the practice of Sadhana. Sadhana is required to quieten your mind and to take you inward.
author: Sri M

text: Smarana means continuously remembering the Name. Not chanting only, but remembering. Japa is chanting. Smarana is remembering. Naamsmarana is remembering a particularly short name or a mantra by which the mind can be engaged within.
author: Sri M

text: The goal is peace of mind, tranquility - finding your True Self within which is connected with the Supreme Being. The way to this is turning your mind within and meditating on the inner, Sadhana is the practice by which you learn how to do this.
author: Sri M

text: The mind does not like to be quiet and calm ever or be in a vacuum. There is no way to suddenly tell the mind to not be engaged. You cannot do it. So engage it in something interior so that it doesn't get time or the opportunity to engage with the outside world, at least for a short while. There are two ways - Naama Smarana and Mantra Japa.
author: Sri M

text: That which cannot be caught by anything is caught by a sound and that sound is Om, the Pranava. And fortunately for us, all of us can chant it. From the external Om, one goes to the internal Om.
author: Sri M

text: Swadharma means the dharma that takes you towards spiritual development and at whatever station in life you are at, do the best thing you can in that station of life to your capacity. You cannot always expect to do perfect, but try to do.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Tantras, Shiva, the Supreme Being resides on the Sahasrara Chakra , with his legs extended downward, touching the bhrumadhya , the center between the eyebrows. The point at which the sushumna nadi enters the Sahasrara Chakra is known in the Tantras as the Brahmarandhra . It is described as the opening or gateway to Brahman, the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: When I sit down to study with my teacher, I should do so with the awareness that I do not know, and therefore I am open to understanding. This does not mean being physically lower. The moment I say, “I know,” all enquiry stops. I can no longer truly hear, because I shut my ears with the feeling that I already know. Even if I do hear, I may interpret what is said according to what I think I know, and this too is dangerous.
author: Sri M

text: Self-realization, Kaivalya or Moksha , does not mean being free from something, but realizing that one is always free but has been labouring under the illusion that one is not. This is the same as ultimate freedom, from which one never falls back to non-freedom or bondage.
author: Sri M

text: Moving up and down the spine is Mukhya Prana , the supreme energy. In yogic terms, this refers to the movement of aspiration, thought, concentration, and energy either toward the higher centers or toward the lower ones. When it moves downward, it leads to material well-being; when it moves upward, it leads to spiritual well-being.
author: Sri M

text: Mantra is a technique, not the goal. When you feel that you have entered a deep state and chanting the mantra requires effort, stop. However, the mind is very subtle and can be deceptive; what appears to be depth may actually be laziness preventing you from chanting. Therefore, examine the situation carefully.
author: Sri M

text: Once all illusions are burnt to ashes, one attains supreme satisfaction, unlimited bliss and happiness. Therefore one has no other desire left. This happens when the Kundalini reaches the ajna chakra , which is the last but one step towards Moksha .
author: Sri M

text: Alchemy is the metaphoric expression of purification of the mind and the soul. The base metal, which is the gross mind, can be refined and made very subtle and pure. Then the same mind is transformed to gold.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Tantras, Kundalini is considered as the manifestation of the infinite supreme energy within the human being . This energy, known as Parashakti or Bhavani, is said to reside in a potent form, not kinetic, but inactive at the base of the spinal cord of all human beings, coiled like a spring. In tantric symbolism, it is depicted as a snake turned three and a half times around itself and waiting to be awakened by the spiritual practitioner.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher teaches a person sadhana according to that person’s capacity and individual needs. Not everyone can practice the same path, because no two people are made in the same way. Some may have a devotional temperament, some an intellectual one, and others may be practitioners of yoga. There are different kinds of people, and accordingly, one has to teach.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities and situations, either deliberately or as they arise naturally. He does not encourage people to run away from situations, but to pause and remain present. It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances that one begins to realize for oneself where one truly stands.
author: Sri M

text: Most of the activities of the world that we perform, based on the assumption that we are the body, bind us down to the earth. Karma Yoga is the theory or teaching which says, that if you can act knowing well that you are actually the supreme ever free self and not the body, then none of these activities can bind you down to sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: We can go anywhere but we carry our mind with us. We can’t escape from the mind. So, the only way, according to the Gita and also according to people who have walked on this path at least to some extent, is to face it, examine it, look at it and handle it. It’s only then you get over it.
author: Sri M

text: A person who has touched that freedom, moksha or mukti, this completeness, lives an unprejudiced life of total freedom not influenced by the stereotyped images that one encounters in day to day life.
author: Sri M

text: You cannot practice freedom because freedom has no design, it has no pattern. It’s absolutely free, unbound, boundless! One cannot ‘practice’ freedom in day to day life.
author: Sri M

text: The whole science of meditation is a way to go beyond or go deeper than the surface of the mind, explore the deeper recesses and come up with greater abilities and greater understanding. So much so that the mind realizes, compared to what it was accustomed to, it has almost reached infinite heights.
author: Sri M

text: Upanishad means that which is taught by the teacher to the student through which he moves closer to The Truth. Upanishad is not in the words, it is in what is transferred between the teacher and the student.
author: Sri M

text: It is possible for someone to lead a life like a normal human being in the material world and, at the same time, keep their spiritual aspirations intact and work in a way that leads to the attainment of spiritual fulfillment.
author: Sri M

text: In spiritual matters, you begin with the understanding that there is something beyond the ordinary mind, and it cannot be known through study. Soaking in the atmosphere of places where the rishis have meditated, which are great centers of energy is the closest you can get. In these places, you simply need to keep quiet and not let the mind interfere, that’s all. Just sit quietly.
author: Sri M

text: It is possible to live in this world and reach one’s spiritual fulfillment at the same time, provided we understand the rules and regulations and the traffic signals to watch out for ; where we can overspeed, where we cannot, the speed limits for travelling in this world, and so on. Then we can use this world as a finishing school to graduate into higher realms of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: I personally don’t think that giving up the world completely, shaving your head to renounce the world and walking away, is the right way to progress on the spiritual path. There have been examples of great saints, great rishis, and great beings who have lived in the world with their families.
author: Sri M

text: When in action, Shakti becomes more powerful, and in calmness, quietness, and tranquillity, Shivam becomes more important.
author: Sri M

text: If you go back to ancient times and look, the concept of Shiva is always constant. It doesn’t come; it doesn’t go. If it has to manifest, it manifests as Shiva. There is no need to change anything, therefore, Shivam. Shivam is a concept of the supreme, original, pure, all-pervading Being, which the Isha Vāsya Upanishad describes as “Ishavasyam Idam Sarvam.” That Supreme Being pervades everything here.
author: Sri M

text: There are many meanings of the word Shivam . One of them is auspiciousness. Wherever there is auspiciousness, there is Shivam . Beauty is Shivam . Absolute purity is Shivam . Light is Shivam . Shivam is also used as a substitute word for Anandam . When you experience the small joys of life, that too is Shivam . When you ultimately experience the bliss of your inner being, that is also Shivam . It is all-pervading. It is in order to find that ultimate Shivam , that we go through the rigmarole of life. You may call it Narayana ; it doesn’t matter. But when I say Shivam , I am referring to the essence of being - completely pure.
author: Sri M

text: Shiva is greatly compassionate and, if necessary, he is also the one who performs the Tandava Nritya . Tandava Nritya is the dance of destruction. For the yogi, Tandava Nritya is the destruction of all that limits the self. The dance of destruction clears away all the accumulated muck. He is Nataraja , the king of dancers. Shiva also represents the dance of life.
author: Sri M

text: In this material world, earning one’s living and going through the problems and travails of mundane, worldly existence is a necessary step in learning about spiritual consciousness and evolution to higher levels.
author: Sri M

text: No amount of bhajans or kirtans is of any use unless the heart changes, unless the heart begins to look beyond oneself. If we can spend even half an hour for others, then we are moving forward.
author: Sri M

text: We often think that only happiness is a blessing. Sorrow is a blessing too; it leads us to greater, deeper, and more permanent happiness. Sometimes, sorrow is given particularly to a person who is on the path, to see how he or she is progressing.
author: Sri M

text: Happiness is a universal pursuit. Whether one is a believer or a non-believer—Hindu, Muslim, Christian, or Sikh - everyone looks for happiness in this world. All our attempts to grasp things and hold on to them are a search for happiness.
author: Sri M

text: When the so-called “limited” being recognises and realises his inner essence, he begins to understand that he is not different from the Absolute.
author: Sri M

text: What is it that one attains in the grihastha period that is different from the brahmacharya period? Once you are married, you have one more person in your life; you cannot take independent or exclusive decisions. You learn to control your emotions, control your anger, and look at the other person’s point of view.
author: Sri M

text: In yogi’s or in a spiritual seeker's mind, manthan happens all the time.
author: Sri M

text: My Master used to say, “When you are alone in a cave, you can say to yourself, ‘I have controlled my emotions; I am not jealous; I am not angry,’ and so on. But the reality is that there is nobody to get angry with and no one to be jealous of.” Things are different when you are in a family.
author: Sri M

text: Perhaps the only way to free the mind from the trappings of the material world is to live in the midst of it, receive guidance from a teacher, and come to terms with the world so that one may transcend it at the proper time.
author: Sri M

text: Living in this world and experiencing life, I would say, is the philosopher’s stone, which can eventually purify you from base metal into pure gold.
author: Sri M

text: When the mind is quiet, it holds tremendous energy. This is not nothingness. It is “no-thing” - that which cannot be defined as a thing. From this, the entire universe arises.
author: Sri M

text: There are wise people who speak very little. In their silence, genius develops.
author: Sri M

text: Try to become spiritual. Try to advance in your spiritual practice.
author: Sri M

text: Kriya means a technique. No technique can find the Truth. Because then it becomes a mechanical thing. But the technique can help you to bring your mind to a certain stage from where it becomes the tarmac for taking off into the higher realms of spirituality. That's all.
author: Sri M

text: If you have everything and if you have not come to terms with the inner reality, then there is no use of all that you have.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is the capacity, consciously developed, to get rid of the vrittis of the chitta. Vrittis are the movement of thoughts, can be good or bad; and Chitta is the mind.
author: Sri M

text: The universal message at the heart of the Hindu teachings, Buddhist teachings, and Christian teachings is Care, Love and Service and to seek peace in the depths of your being. As it is said 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God.
author: Sri M

text: Self-observation is good, and it helps us grow, but not self-criticism. If you criticize yourself all the time, there is no way you can improve yourself. However much you fall, get up and get going.
author: Sri M

text: When you reach the core where you are all settled, then whether you are supported by your family and friends or not, you can handle it. This is my understanding and my experience. It has to do with yourself, not with the other person. If you are okay, then the other person will fall into place. If you are not, and you keep pushing, then it's not going to work.
author: Sri M

text: Swadhyaya means to do self study and also to study the self. Studying oneself is not simply hearing or reading something; it involves exploring your inner being and finding out how it affects you.
author: Sri M

text: You know how powerful words are! So, watch yourself. Be careful of what you say. Ninety percent of the troubles in this world, for us, are caused by not talking responsibly.
author: Sri M

text: This human body and this human world into which we come are full of sorrow from all sides. Since it is the only vehicle which leads us on to moksha, it is very precious.
author: Sri M

text: As your feelings become more and more subtle, deeper centers of the human mind open up to form a link to that which is beyond the ordinary mind.
author: Sri M

text: The Bhagavad Gita itself is an upanishad or the essence of all the Upanishads put in simple language, for a layman to understand.
author: Sri M

text: In the Gita, the chapter after Arjuna Vishada Yoga is Sankhya Yoga , the Yoga of knowledge. So, seeing that Arjuna is in sorrow, and observing the miserable state he has gone into, Krishna explains to him and begins the teaching of the knowledge required to handle this sorrow.
author: Sri M

text: The first thing that happens as one advances in sadhana is that one develops compassion in the heart.
author: Sri M

text: Vedanta is not intellectual acrobatics. You can stand on your head. You can study all the scriptures. You can know them by heart. But, unless and until, the quality of mind improves, one cannot find the truth. And how does it improve? By understanding that one (is not in control).
author: Sri M

text: Every practitioner of spiritual exercise should keep in mind -that when you practice and go deeper and deeper, all the tendencies that have been hidden in your subconscious mind till now-bottled up – they will all come to the surface. That is the poison. That is where you might get some help from a teacher, who knows how to handle it, otherwise, everything can go berserk.
author: Sri M

text: Is a Guru necessary to attain freedom? Does the Guru induce freedom? If the Guru is inducing freedom, it cannot be freedom. It can only be something similar to freedom.
author: Sri M

text: The rising of the kundalini therefore is the rising of consciousness from the gross to the subtle, subtler and subtler levels until It reaches the highest stage in the sahasraara chakra and the yogi enters into a deep trance which is an altered state of consciousness.
author: Sri M

text: Intelligence has to realize that from a point, it’s function is over and allow something else to take over. That instrument of perception that takes over is known as intuition, Jnana Drishti.
author: Sri M

text: Babaji used to say, ‘The seeds have been planted, they have been sown but no seed will become a tree and bear fruit in three days, it takes its own time’. So sow the seed, keep the climate clear, water it properly and then we’ll see what happens.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of yoga is the way of finding that happiness which is our true identity. We discover that we are not what we think we are, but something entirely different. Swami Vivekananda explained it beautifully. He said, “We are hypnotised by the false happiness that the world seems to give us. We have to de-hypnotise ourselves and come back to our senses.
author: Sri M

text: You have a slate and you write on it. Every time you write on it, if you want to write anything else, you have to rub it off. Otherwise you can neither read it, nor is there space to write anything more. So in matters of inner exploration, the most important thing is to keep your slate clean.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t carry your anger and hatred, stupidity and poisonous feelings against others from one day to the next. When we go to sleep, can we leave it there and get up fresh in the morning and say, ‘That’s okay. Yesterday is over’.
author: Sri M

text: Shraddha has several meanings but one of the meanings is complete attention - total one-pointed attention.
author: Sri M

text: The experience of happiness is innate, not in the object that l enjoy. The object may although be necessary to excite it or bring it out. Therefore, Vedanta says - the source of all happiness is within us. When you are in contact with certain objects, this innate happiness is aroused within us.
author: Sri M

text: In the Yoga Vasistha, Vasistha says to Rama, “A person who thinks everything is destined and doesn't put in any self-effort is equivalent to a donkey.” We always say it’s destiny when there is something we can't do. When we can do it, we think we did it. So instead of thinking about whether it is destiny or not, if you have an aim, you should put in a lot of effort into it. If constant effort doesn't work, then you can say, “Oh, this is destiny.
author: Sri M

text: There is happiness and complete fulfillment available to every human being within oneself and independent of anything outside. The search just has to be reversed to look within.
author: Sri M

text: The best sign of your progress in your meditation is something very self-evident. Nobody has to tell you what's happening. First is the experience of great bliss; the second is the actual experience of your Being. It's not just a little sensation but an expansion throughout the Being in all ways, and not merely a physical expansion. It's an expansion in all forms, in all ways.
author: Sri M

text: Questions never end. When you figure out that questions are part of the movement of the mind, and when everything is still, there is nothing left to ask. This is something that has to happen on its own. It's not something that can be imposed on anybody.
author: Sri M

text: The Gita says that he who has conquered his mind, which means he does not let the desperate, dejected mind take hold, and who has succeeded, through practice (abhyasa) , in keeping a positive mind most of the time, such a mind remains steady and unperturbed in pleasure or pain.
author: Sri M

text: The true Self is already purified. There is nothing to purify. It's the mind that covers it that needs to be purified.
author: Sri M

text: If you have faith in an infinite Supreme Being, put all your heart into what you want to do or achieve.
author: Sri M

text: Sit down and meditate in your heart center and whenever such thoughts come which are not related to the inner, try to keep them away.
author: Sri M

text: I decided, ‘I am walking on this path, it’s a lonely path’. Like Jesus Christ said, 'It’s a straight and narrow path’. So, let’s stick to it and not get side-tracked.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth.
author: Sri M

text: Jesus said the real treasure is in your heart where thieves do not break in and steal; It is this treasure that we seek.
author: Sri M

text: If the world were a complete obstruction to the attainment of spiritual fulfillment, the Supreme Being would not have created it at all. The world exists around us and also in our minds to make us understand, learn, grow and become complete.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t run away from the battle. Stay there and fight it out – but with love, affection, and understanding.
author: Sri M

text: I think all the sadhana we do is intended to mostly bring about the hunger for God – for that Truth. When that hunger has built up, then God is at your doorstep!
author: Sri M

text: Surrender means to understand that I am helpless at a certain point and, therefore, I need to relax, let go, be patient and wait. In that waiting, something arrives. The breeze may be from within.
author: Sri M

text: Any place, where the truth is worshipped, is a temple for us. The most important temple is the body. Inside us is the heart where the Truth sits.
author: Sri M

text: A small good deed, a kind deed done to another human being or another living creature, can wipe out the dirt of negativity that has gathered in your soul and make it free and clear as a mirror to reflect Divinity.
author: Sri M

text: When you enter the meditation hall, leave your ego outside along with your shoes; don’t bring it in. Go inside like a new-born child who is free - you have no enemies, you don’t hate anybody, at least for the time being.
author: Sri M

text: Once you learn the art of being one pointed in meditation or in day to day life, you are automatically in a meditative state all the time.
author: Sri M

text: When one is established in deep silence, then no noise can disturb you. Silence is not the absence of sound. In the depths of your heart, there is silence. You sometimes come upon it when you look at the lake or the mountain.
author: Sri M

text: If you are seeking a spiritual teacher, get rid of the conventional ideas you may have about a teacher, because that prejudice may prevent you from seeing a real teacher.
author: Sri M

text: Think outside the box. Don’t go solely on linear logic; use fuzzy logic. Turn things upside down and look, you will see things are quite different.
author: Sri M

text: No one can spiritually advance by simply sitting down cross-legged and meditating 24 hours. The moment you begin to see divinity in all living beings and start serving human beings, the mind can begin to purify and reach higher states. Service is an important part of Sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: In each individual’s spiritual journey, the pace may differ. There are many influences and reasons, so one should never give up. Carry on!
author: Sri M

text: To be spiritual does not mean to become weak. Forgiveness is a great strength. It’s the weak who cannot forgive.
author: Sri M

text: When the love for the Divine arises, it’s like an overflow. There are no questions.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t go to extremes. If you go to one extreme in this world, you might get thrown to the other. Moderation is the key.
author: Sri M

text: Yoga is not a passive state. It is a super-active state wherein there's action in the tranquillity of mind, without agitation.
author: Sri M

text: It doesn’t matter who the teacher is, what he or she looks like, etc. What's important is the wisdom that comes from the teacher.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual seeker is not tempted by anything other than to find the truth one-pointedly.
author: Sri M

text: When you become more mindful of yourself, you become more mindful of the outer world.
author: Sri M

text: The highest knowledge is that which leads you to the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: The Truth that we seek, is almost like no-thing. Which is why the Buddha called it Shunya. When my ego becomes zero, then I see that zero. That Nothing is the essence of everything.
author: Sri M

text: According to the Buddha, desire is the root of all sorrow and freedom from desire is freedom from sorrow for all mankind.
author: Sri M

text: Some great spiritual teachers are so absorbed in the fullness just like a full vessel. There is no sound; there’s no need to speak.
author: Sri M

text: Deep down, the preparation is to create space, to empty our prejudices and be free. This preparation can be done in any tradition, but without space, nothing can be received.
author: Sri M

text: When there is too much undigested philosophical information or when the mind is obsessed and restless all the time, it leaves no room to receive anything from the infinite. The wounds, hurts, and hatred we carry in our hearts are the greatest barriers. They are the muck that fills us up. Unless this muck is cleaned, there is no space for anything real to happen. And when this space is created, we realize that everything we seek has always been within us.
author: Sri M

text: There is this constant desire to be complete, to be full. This is how life moves, and we never seem to find this completeness outside. If it can be found inside, you will see it reflected outside.
author: Sri M

text: That completeness comes when our little selfish personality that is only thinking about me and myself has gone. When I think only of ‘you’, your pain becomes my pain. It’s no longer localized. Your happiness is my happiness. This is not theory or philosophy; it’s the experience of those who have touched that completeness.
author: Sri M

text: The greatest dharma is not to hurt or injure others, and cause no grief to others. Have affection towards everyone. This is the complete definition of dharma.
author: Sri M

text: The most important function of the Guru is to act as a well-polished mirror so that we see ourselves as we are, with all our imperfections. The teacher reflects what is going on in us.
author: Sri M

text: You need to practise. The approach does not matter. Results come with constant practice. This helps you maintain your spiritual journey without disruption.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam means consciousness, bliss, and auspiciousness. It is present within us and moving towards it is the spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: The ‘you do for me’ should go and be replaced with ‘I do for myself’. Practice! Your practice is your experience.
author: Sri M

text: Money is not everything. It can buy many things, but it cannot buy happiness or fulfillment.
author: Sri M

text: A Sthitaprajna is one whose state of mind has become balanced, steady, and unruffled, yet is still active.
author: Sri M

text: When all the desires of the heart have been understood and let go of, and when the spirit finds joy and satisfaction in itself without any external add-ons, then one is a person with steady wisdom.
author: Sri M

text: Whether on the path of self-realisation or not, you should think that things will happen at the right time. Keep working; patience is of essence.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t go to extremes. If you go to one extreme in this world, you might get thrown to the other. Moderation is the key.
author: Sri M

text: The idea of looking within is to close one's eyes, look into the mind, and see how it's functioning. There are hundreds of thoughts in there. Keep observing them with the belief that, one day, these thoughts will cease. Then, there's a chance of getting in touch with the core of your being.
author: Sri M

text: When internal churning is on, that’s the time when you should not fall victim to it or get addicted to it. Instead, watch it, and it'll subside. Then, comes the amrita or nectar.
author: Sri M

text: If the body has not rested and is not alert, then it cannot meditate. It'll impact the mind. So, keep your body in a state where it's not tortured by lack of sleep or extreme fasting.
author: Sri M

text: Once the mind becomes disciplined, then it can be established solely on the inner Self. When it is free from the longing for other things, only then, you are free.
author: Sri M

text: Even if you touch a tiny part of what's within - the real, conscious, bliss, Ananda, then you can sail through life because your treasure is within you. This treasure is source of the entire universe.
author: Sri M

text: One of the biggest problems we face when we sit down to meditate is distraction. If we don’t fix a daily schedule, success is not possible. The mind, out of habit, runs in various directions; you should be able to catch and fix it.
author: Sri M

text: Is there some way by which the ordinary mind, caught up in this world with its pains and pleasures, can be free and touch the essence? The study of this is called the Brahmavidya, and the way to do this is called Yoga.
author: Sri M

text: If you have kissed the garment of Truth, then you see the universal in even the mundane. You see the heart; you don’t see anything else.
author: Sri M

text: Sadhana is to prepare the mind towards the extraordinary. And, perhaps then, it gets a glimpse of the Truth.
author: Sri M

text: Satsang is a group of people trying to find the Truth. You and I are going to look at the problem together.
author: Sri M

text: When all supports fail, then there is That—the Ultimate support.
author: Sri M

text: Devotion is required to move on the spiritual path, besides a rough understanding of what we are doing and why we are doing it. But it cannot be cultivated.
author: Sri M

text: Being truthful and honest is a prerequisite for any spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: Ultimately, you are your own Master. There is no other. A teacher can help you understand this point. If you do, then you are free. My job is to tell you that your teacher is in you.
author: Sri M

text: Nobody can give us illumination; we have to find it ourselves. Just as one who is hungry has to find food for oneself.
author: Sri M

text: We carry so many things in our head. Be simple. Throw off the burdens and be free!
author: Sri M

text: If you are on the spiritual path, moving towards the Truth, the first step is try to be truthful in day-to-day life. You cannot tell lies 24 hours a day and expect to find the Absolute Truth.
author: Sri M

text: No matter what happens, don’t bother. You may suffer losses, or you may get into trouble. Stick to your spiritual path, if you are serious.
author: Sri M

text: When you find a spiritual teacher, ask for the real thing. Don’t ask for the petty stuff. Sometimes in trouble, one asks for such things, it’s okay. However, always keep in mind that what you have to look for is That.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t be afraid of being left alone. It’s beautiful, that’s the time when you talk to yourself. That’s also when you talk to your God. When left alone, that's the time you can look into yourself and find out where your problems are. So, appreciate it when you are alone and be thankful to those who have let you be alone.
author: Sri M

text: Knowing oneself starts with knowing oneself in the midst of people, not alone. In seclusion, I don’t see how I am. We should first know who we are and where we stand. To know thyself means knowing myself as I am, instead of just repeating ‘I am the Brahman’! I can’t be angry, jealous, narrow and still be Brahman.
author: Sri M

text: Peace is a state of mind that emerges from within. If I am not peaceful with myself, then I cannot bring peace anywhere.
author: Sri M

text: Each one of us, with our limitations, needs to understand the fact of how we are related to this world, and how, while we are still in this world, can free ourselves from it.
author: Sri M

text: If your search for the Truth is serious, then the right kind of guidance will come in some way. You have to remain sincere.
author: Sri M

text: If you are seeking a spiritual teacher, get rid of the conventional ideas you may have about a teacher, because that prejudice may prevent you from seeing a real teacher.
author: Sri M

text: In the process of delving into the mind, there is a lot of churning. When you churn, just like the ancient ‘Samudra Manthan’ (churning of the ocean), the first thing that emerges is poison. Unfortunately for us, there is no Shiva around to consume it. This poison must appear first and, then only will the Amrit (nectar) come.
author: Sri M

text: When emotions come, don’t run away from them. Feel what is happening. Being emotional human beings, we cannot discover ourselves in a ‘dry’ emotionless manner. Only when we experience emotions are we human beings. That's when we can look at ourselves to learn and understand who we are.
author: Sri M

text: While you are on the spiritual journey, two essential steps have to go side-by-side. One, is sitting down and doing your sadhana; the other is to examine your life - see what you are and how you behave with people.
author: Sri M

text: We need eyes to see an object. But we cannot see our own eyes except as a reflection in a mirror. Yet, we cannot say that the eye does not exist. It is because of the fact that the eye exists, we see things around us; similarly the ‘Atman’ or Consciousness. It is only because of this root identity that we are ‘alive’ and ‘conscious’. To realize this true identity is the main purpose of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: Krishna represents love, thus love is a comprehensive panacea for all ills. If you really understand it’s meaning which is utter selflessness, not love for my own sake but love for Love’s sake, only then, it is a panacea for all problems. This is very rare. When Kabir Das wove, everyone thought he was weaving cloth. Actually, he was weaving from the warp and weft of love and devotion.
author: Sri M

text: Energy - once its work of creation, preservation, and destruction is done, still remains whole. This is not possible when we think of energy in the daily world. We work and we feel tired. We say, 'some of my energy is lost'. But here, the whole Cosmos is spun out of this energy, which keeps working tirelessly and yet remains unaltered.
author: Sri M

text: Live with the understanding that the entire universe is pervaded by that blissful Supreme Being and we are a part of that! This is not a fantasy that needs to be worked out in our minds. It is a fact and the actual process through which it is possible is known as sadhana or meditation.
author: Sri M

text: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna tells Arjuna that one of the most important qualities of a devotee of mine is 'sarva bhoota hitey rataha' - compassion for all beings. Here, Krishna is not speaking as Krishna, a person, but as the manifestation of the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: There’s an English saying – 'blind leading the blind’. It is an ancient statement and comes from the Mundaka Upanishad – ‘andhenaiva nīyamānā yathāndhāḥ.‘ It refers to those who have learnt only theoretically and think they know. When such people lead others into spiritual matters, it is like the blind leading the blind.
author: Sri M

text: The practice of yoga is the way of finding that happiness which is our true identity. We discover that we are not what we think we are, but something entirely different.
author: Sri M

text: Experiencing life through the sorrows and pleasures, the pains and happiness that the body and the mind go through, one evolves into a better and cleaner entity before it touches a level that cannot even be called human, but divine.
author: Sri M

text: When I wake up in the morning, the first thing that I recognise is that I exist. And then the world exists. I see everything around. But that first feeling that ‘I am’, that awareness that ‘I am consciousness’ bereft of ‘I am this’ or ‘I am that’ in its pure form is what we mean by the ‘atman’.
author: Sri M

text: Sai Baba of Shirdi would say ‘Allah Malik Hai,’ or ‘Ram, Ram’ when people went to him with their problems. No one could say whether he was a Muslim, Hindu, or a Christian. His basic message was to unite, to bring people together, because Allah and Ram to Him were the same, though we call God by different names.
author: Sri M

text: Satsang is critical because you become the company you keep. If I live with people who talk about the Truth or want to find out what it is; who do japa and kirtan and bhajan, then I will become like them in due course. It may take time. If I continue to live with people who are planning which drink to have next, I will become like that. It is but natural.
author: Sri M

text: While we practice our sadhana, if we sometimes get some powers, see lights or hear sounds, do not think that God is going to come! There are many people who have many powers, but have not yet had the darshan of the Lord. It is not the same; it could also be separate. There may be someone who shows no capacity for the so-called ‘siddhis’, but might have had the darshan of the Lord.
author: Sri M

text: Every day when you wake up in the morning, or go to bed at night, look at yourself and say, ‘where am I, what am I doing? How many falsities are still in my life? Am I really doing my sadhana sincerely?’ People say - I don’t have time. We have time for everything else. The fact is that urgency for sadhana has not arrived.
author: Sri M

text: In your relationship with the spiritual teacher, please be frank, truthful and clear. Don’t try to bluff, because it does not work. The teacher may not tell you so, but he knows and understands. So, be very frank.
author: Sri M

text: Can there be knowledge of that which ‘Is’? When we try to understand this with our conditioned brain, we gain the insight that all things one gathers in one’s head are a memory. And if it is a memory, it is something in the past, and if it is something in the past, it cannot be the reality that is always the present.
author: Sri M

text: The human brain somehow seems to be wired for spiritual experience. Certain centers in the brain become active when you are in deep meditation. These are the centers that yoga and Vedanta have talked about.
author: Sri M

text: Every day is a new day. It's not as if you have discovered, and you're finished, and it's gone. Every day there is an unveiling happening and it happens in different ways.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual being is one who keeps doing his work, not worrying too much about the results. You need to have a goal, but if it doesn't work, move forward, don’t hang on to that.
author: Sri M

text: Inner growth is reflected and is shown by the way we act and behave with people who are close to us – when we reflect this, not what we wish to project.
author: Sri M

text: Let us not think that we cannot do much – let us say, ‘let us do something,’ And that ‘something’ should start in here, in the heart.
author: Sri M

text: Anyone who has touched the amrita, even a drop of it, or half a drop of it, becomes so intoxicated and filled with the joy of Shivam, that nothing else is an attraction to him.
author: Sri M

text: We can go anywhere but we carry our mind with us. We can’t escape from the mind. So, face it, examine it, look at it and handle it. It’s only then you get over it.
author: Sri M

text: In the pilgrimage of life, stick to the truth as far as possible.
author: Sri M

text: The most important thing to remember is kindness and compassion towards others.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever be the activity you are involved in, don't forget to remember at least for a few minutes in the evening that there is a Supreme Reality behind the whole universe.
author: Sri M

text: If you want to be free of ignorance, you need knowledge. But once you are free, you have to throw both away. Don’t stick the thorn of knowledge into your foot and think ‘I know everything’.
author: Sri M

text: Devotion is spontaneous. We can teach all the ways leading to it but what it is, can’t be taught. Suddenly, the seed sprouts; we don’t know how. It sprouts in different ways for different people.
author: Sri M

text: Sometimes it is difficult for us to distinguish what is real and what is unreal. For that, we need maximum alertness, which develops as part of our sadhana.
author: Sri M

text: A person whose mind is completely and totally on the path, he will do only what is right and forget about the rest! But it is not so easy. It can come only with spiritual maturity.
author: Sri M

text: The evolved human being is not judged by the number of cars he owns or the dollars in his bank balance. The hallmark of an evolved being is the quality of his heart - love, understanding and a strong desire for peace.
author: Sri M

text: Bhajan is not just chanting or singing. It means to completely absorb yourself in the Inner. It is actually a spiritual version of bhojan for the physical body. So it is a bhojan for the mind.
author: Sri M

text: Whatever happens, even if you are sick, try not to miss the routine practice of meditation.
author: Sri M

text: Layers of prejudice close the eyes, ears, and heart. When the wind blows, nothing can enter. So, all the practices we do are meant to open the windows to the heart.
author: Sri M

text: There is a divinity in every heart, and that divinity - by its very essence - is peace, tranquility, and happiness. The more you tune into it, the happier you are, the better your mind is, and the better you function in your relationship with others.
author: Sri M

text: Don't be obsessed with failure. All people who have succeeded are those who have failed and continued and said we will somehow do it.
author: Sri M

text: There are some people who seem to be happy in all situations because they have found out through experiences of life that the peace, tranquility and happiness that they seek is inside, not outside.
author: Sri M

text: In life we go through all circumstances. Sometimes there is happiness, sometimes there is sorrow. Sometimes people blame you, sometimes they praise you. The yogi is one who considers praise and blame as equal. He is not moved by it.
author: Sri M

text: Half an hour or one hour of sitting down quietly and being mindful of your mind, thoughts and breath is a very important preparation to attain that mindfulness which we seek, which is to be totally free of all this.
author: Sri M

text: Because you are emotional, it doesn’t mean that you should not maintain tranquility. Your emotions should be directed towards achieving your goal, rather than in other things.
author: Sri M

text: When you live in this world be aware of how you behave. Be mindful of what you do in the outside world, be mindful of your inner world and one day what will remain is only the witness, the sakshi which is the seer. This is kaivalya.
author: Sri M

text: When the ordinary thinking or the ordinary rational logic subsides, then comes the feeling called Bhakti. Bhakti is not different from Jnana Yoga but it’s that which comes with feelings not words, sound or music.
author: Sri M

text: Following the teachings is more important than worshipping the Teacher.
author: Sri M

text: When you say Guru, it means a teacher in all ways; could be a small child who teaches you innocence of childhood, it could be a philosophical teacher who teaches you the Upanishads, they are all Gurus.
author: Sri M

text: The function of the Guru is to show a mirror to you. To clean the mirror and show it properly at the right angle so that you see yourself as you actually are, not what you want to be.
author: Sri M

text: It is the function of the Outer Guru, a teacher, to bring about the development of the student so that he / she becomes more reliant on the Inner Guru than the Outer Guru. The Outer Guru can disappear, but the Inner does not. The Inner Guru is actually none other than the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: As you journey on the path, the more you desire, the more is your aspiration towards having a glimpse of the Supreme, then something very soft and nice grows in your heart. It's very fragrant. And when it grows, that is devotion.
author: Sri M

text: When you have gone deep enough in your meditation, in your spiritual practice, you are not aware of the outside world in a state of deep trance, you are not even thinking of any idea what you should do or what you should not do, suddenly a thought will come into your mind. You may not even have thought about it and it's not even from your subconscious. It comes deep from within and then you know, yes, this is to be done, then it's your inner Guru speaking. It may not even be speaking in words. It may be suddenly that you realize, I know this.
author: Sri M

text: Be a bhakta - devotee more than anything else because through bhakti all jnana - wisdom will dawn.
author: Sri M

text: We have the most complex brain, better than any other animals therefore we tend to think that it is because of this that everything is functioning. Consciousness can be totally free of the brain and act on its own if required.
author: Sri M

text: When you practice the techniques taught through the spiritual texts, you will come to a stage where your mind is no more limited to the brain but is multidimensional.
author: Sri M

text: When you practice the techniques taught through the spiritual texts, you will come to a stage where your mind is no more limited to the brain but is multidimensional.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities and situations, either deliberately or as they happen. He does not encourage people to run away from situations but to pause and remain. It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

text: A spiritual teacher sometimes provides opportunities and situations, either deliberately or as they happen. He does not encourage people to run away from situations but to pause and remain. It is only when faced with a particular set of circumstances, one begins to realise for oneself where one stands.
author: Sri M

text: Moving up and down the spine is Mukhya Prana, the Supreme energy. In yogic terms, it is the movement of the aspiration, thought, concentration and energy towards either the higher side or the lower side. When it goes down it leads to material wellbeing. When it goes up, it leads to Spiritual wellbeing.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam cannot be touched without the activation of the Shakti. Without the havan kund, no homa can be done.
author: Sri M

text: Mantra is a technique and not the goal. When you feel you have entered a deep state and chanting the mantra also takes effort, Stop! But watch out, the mind is very tricky, it may be laziness which may be preventing you from chanting. So, examine carefully.
author: Sri M

text: Once all illusions are burnt to ashes, one arrives at supreme satisfaction, unlimited bliss and happiness. Therefore one has no other desire left. This happens when the Kundalini reaches the ajna chakra, which is the last but one step towards Moksha.
author: Sri M

text: When you enter the meditation hall, leave your shoes outside along with your ego; don’t bring it in. Go inside like a new-born child who is free, you have no enemies, you don’t hate anybody, at least for the time being. This is easier said than done but it’s the easiest way to bring about a completely tranquil and deep meditative mind.
author: Sri M

text: Remove all the conditions that are there and remain in that One essential state. This is the aim of the Vedantic teaching. One discovers that one is not this body nor the mind but the inner self, the atman which is free of all unhappiness and which by essential nature is Sat Chit Ananda, or true happiness.
author: Sri M

text: Freedom is our birthright. Our true self, the atman is free; it does not need to be freed from anything. It is free because it is complete, ‘purna’. ‘Purnamadah’ - That completeness is actually ‘you’ in your true essence.
author: Sri M

text: What is that one attains in the grihastha period which is different from the brahmacharya period? Once you are married you have one more person in your life; you cannot take independent and exclusive decisions. You learn to control your emotions, control your anger and to look at the other person’s point of view
author: Sri M

text: According to Vedanta that feeling of being dependent on what is around you, the feeling that you are bound and that you have to get out of it, is part of the great illusion of the mind called the Maya.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t unnecessarily complicate life with too many things. Speak the truth; More than speaking the truth, think the truth. That does not mean that when you speak the truth you have to be blunt. There are sweet ways of speaking the truth. You need not be brusque and then suffer because of that.
author: Sri M

text: If you need to understand the essence of the teachings of this country, which is also universal, Lokah samastah sukhino bhavantu, you have to go to the Upanishads.
author: Sri M

text: No sacrifice is a sacrifice if you are not giving what is closest to you, with a full heart. That's not a sacrifice.
author: Sri M

text: The wise look for the good and don't care for the pleasant. Fools look for the pleasant and forget the good. They fall for the pleasant and forget what is good, because the good may not always be pleasant. Choose the good in preference to the pleasant.
author: Sri M

text: We think that we are advancing, improving, when there is plenty, goodness and when there is happiness. It's pain and sorrow that makes us move forward. When that comes, don't try to run and say, take it off! It will be taken off if you say, take it off. But one would not have learned the lesson, why it is there, why has it come.
author: Sri M

text: Under all circumstances, keep your mind peaceful, quiet, tranquil. Because action that comes out of a tranquil mind is usually the right action. Action that comes out of an agitated mind cannot be proper action.
author: Sri M

text: I know people who have billions or more, but they are not happy. If we think that because somebody has a lot of money, that person is happy, we are labouring under a big illusion. There are people who have nothing and are happy. So, the happiness quotient does not depend on what you have and what you don't have. It is the blessing of the Supreme Being.
author: Sri M

text: The morning one and the evening sandhya are very important times when we should remember our link and connection with the Supreme Being. If we do that, throughout the day whatever work we do, whatever joys we get, and whatever pains we experience, all these will be set in a proper order.
author: Sri M

text: When happiness comes, don’t get too excited. And when pain comes, don’t get too depressed. To stay in this state at all times, is the meaning of the word Sthitaprajna, in the Gita.
author: Sri M

text: Sarvatra Samabuddhaya - under any circumstances, meditating, not meditating, walking, eating, working, can I keep my mind tranquil and not agitated? If this is possible, then we are leading a spiritual life. If this is not possible, whatever rituals you do, whatever yoga you practice, you may stand for two hours on your head and wave your legs in the sky, you are not leading a spiritual life.
author: Sri M

text: Spiritual life is to anchor oneself on the divinity of the Supreme Being in your heart, by constantly remembering that even breathing which keeps us alive, is not in our hands.
author: Sri M

text: To be spiritual is not to run away from life. You cannot run away anywhere, your mind is also going with you. The process, the repair work that has to happen is in the mind. We need to work out ways and means by which in the turmoil of this world, the mind remains tranquil.
author: Sri M

text: Keep the mind tranquil under all circumstances, not only when I sit down to meditate. If you don't keep your mind tranquil, an agitated mind functioning in this world brings about more agitation than calmness.
author: Sri M

text: Shivam means consciousness, bliss, and auspiciousness. It is present within us and moving towards it is the spiritual journey.
author: Sri M

text: Grace is not absent, it's always there. We don't open our windows to let it in. It's like the gentle breeze that blows outside. Our windows and doors are closed, it doesn't come in. Keep them open, so that the grace that is always around us flows into our heart.
author: Sri M

text: What you seek is right within you, but we search for it everywhere but in us. Inside us, there is a beautiful treasure which we tend to miss.
author: Sri M

text: Don’t run away from the battle. You cannot run anywhere. So stay here and fight it out but do it with love and affection and understanding. See Krishna in everybody.
author: Sri M

text: Janamashtami is a day to actually rejoice for the advent of spiritual consciousness on earth, in a very complete and all embracing form.
author: Sri M

text: If your search for the Truth is serious, then the right kind of guidance will come in some way. You have to remain sincere.
author: Sri M
